proof_roadmap: Triple dictionary (proof lines 551-557).

metadata.title: Bi-anti-symmetry identity for the double Vandermonde-type product
authors: Priddis, Nathan, Shoemaker, Mark, Wen, Yaoxiong

statement_spans.label: author Lemma environment with its own label l:sym (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 1617-1622

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the Lemma: sets L and R to the two sides of the identity; shows R is divisible by each (z_i - z_l) by pairing each permutation sigma with sigma composed with the transposition (il), whose terms cancel upon the substitution z_i = z_l = z, and symmetrically divisible by each (x_i - x_l); since deg R = r(r-1), R equals a constant times L, and the constant is fixed by comparing the coefficient of the monomial (z_i x_i)^(i-1), which in R appears only in the sigma = id summand with coefficient (-1)^(r(r-1)/2) by induction and in L arises from the displayed product, matching (source lines 1624-1645)

core_obligations: Pairing argument: R is divisible by each (z_i - z_l), i != l (proof lines 1627-1636).
Symmetric argument: R is divisible by each (x_i - x_l) (proof lines 1638-1641).
Degree count forces R = constant * L (proof line 1642).
Coefficient comparison on (z_i x_i)^(i-1) fixes the constant (proof lines 1643-1645).
proof_roadmap: Divisibility in the z-variables (proof lines 1627-1636).
Divisibility in the x-variables (proof lines 1638-1641).
Degree and constant (proof lines 1642-1645).
metadata.difficulty_reason: Complete symmetric-function argument with the pairing, degree and coefficient steps all displayed; the auxiliary induction is stated with its one-line mechanism; no omissions, no citations.

metadata.title: Homotopy of the analytic-continuation path into the equal-Novikov diagonal
authors: Priddis, Nathan, Shoemaker, Mark, Wen, Yaoxiong

statement_spans.label: author Proposition environment with its own label p:ancon (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 1414-1422

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the Proposition: defines the function f of q_{k,+} via the displayed gamma/Pi product, shows it solves a first-order Fuchsian differential equation with singularities at 0, infinity and (-1)^(n-r+1); the product over k of the f's is acted on by the differential operator Delta-hat giving K^+, so K^+ has the same logarithmic poles; Figures f1/f2/f3 then walk the path of analytic continuation homotopically away from the pole hyperplanes: first the projections of the concatenated path are deformed (Figure 2), then the real parts of the coordinates are made equal (Figure 3), so the resulting path gamma-hat lies entirely in the diagonal q_{1,+} = ... = q_{r,+}, within the analyticity domain and independently of beta and delta^+, which yields the specialized continuation identity e:CHspecial (source lines 1423-1575)

core_obligations: Presentation: express the fixed locus as the GIT quotient of the space of morphisms from the sum of the line bundles to the trivial bundle twisted by the representation, with respect to the stability parameter (proof lines 432-435)
Tautological map: over the quotient stack there is a tautological map of vector bundles from the pullback of the sum of the line bundles to the dual of the tautological bundle (proof lines 436-442)

Identification: the locus where that map is an isomorphism is exactly the stable locus, which gives the stated splitting of the restriction for one sign of the parameter, and the other case is the same argument (proof lines 443-444 with 424-427)
proof_roadmap: Write the fixed locus B_{delta^-} as the GIT quotient of Hom(sum MB_{delta^-_i}, O_B tensor C^r) by G with respect to theta_-.
Over the quotient stack there is a tautological map q^*(sum MB_{delta^-_i}) -> R^vee; the locus where it is an isomorphism is by definition the theta_-stable locus.
Hence on the stable locus the restriction of R splits as the sum of the duals of the MB_{delta^-_i}, which is the first assertion; the second assertion is proved in the same way with the other sign.

core_obligations: Vanishing: the classes pulled back from the base and twisted by the idempotents restrict to zero on every other fixed locus, by the restriction statement for the tautological bundle (proof line 599)

The localization theorem in K-theory (as in the cited works) then gives that the classes span the localized equivariant K-theory.

core_obligations: Reduction: by the spanning statement for the localized equivariant K-theory and the projection formula it suffices to check the commutativity on the class attached to a parameter (proof lines 680-682)
Computation of both sides: the Chern character of the restriction of that class to either fixed locus is computed explicitly as a product of binomial factors (proof lines 683-699)
Ratio: after identifying the two fixed loci the ratio of the two expressions simplifies to the transition factor appearing in the statement of the transform (proof lines 700-705)
Conclusion: the localization theorem in cohomology then gives the commutativity of the diagram (proof line 706)
proof_roadmap: It suffices to prove ch(FM(e_{delta^-})) = UU_H(ch(e_{delta^-})), since the general case follows by the spanning statement and the projection formula.
Compute ch(i_{delta^-}^* e_{delta^-}) and ch(i_{delta^+}^* FM(e_{delta^-})) as products of binomial factors in the Chern roots.
Their ratio, after identifying the two fixed loci B_{delta^-} and B_{delta^+}, is precisely the factor C_{delta^-,delta^+} appearing in the definition of the cohomological transform.
The localization theorem in cohomology (cited) then implies that the square commutes.

core_obligations: Rewrite the continued invariant as a pairing: the definition of the genus zero invariant writes it as the symplectic pairing of the continued I-function with the image of the class (proof line 1763)

Apply the diagram and the symplectic property: the diagram of the preceding theorem identifies the first argument with the transform of the other I-function and the symplectic property transfers the pairing to the other side (proof lines 1764-1765)
Read off the statement: the resulting pairing is exactly the genus zero invariant of the original class on the other side (proof line 1766)
proof_roadmap: Write the continued invariant as the pairing of the continued I-function with the image of the class under the transform.

Use the commutative diagram of the theorem to replace the first argument by the transform of the other I-function, and the preservation of the symplectic pairing to move the whole pairing to the other side.
The resulting expression is by definition the genus zero invariant of the original class, which is the assertion.
